skill.name: Agent Browser
skill.description: Command-driven browser automation for AI agents, including navigation, page inspection, form interaction, screenshots, and session workflows.
skill.summary: Automates browser navigation, interaction, page inspection, and screenshots through structured CLI commands.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: The skill is legitimate browser automation documentation, but several instructions create material security risk. The main issues are real Chrome profile reuse, remote debugging of authenticated sessions, persistent OAuth cookies, and commands that can access browser cookies or local storage.

remediation.issue: Real Chrome profile reuse with remote debugging
remediation.suggestion: Remove instructions that attach automation to a real profile. Recommend isolated test profiles and require explicit user confirmation for any authenticated profile use.
Replace the named local profile path with a generic placeholder and avoid publishing personal filesystem paths.
Warn users to use staging accounts, limited permissions, and isolated browser sessions for OAuth workflows.

remediation.issue: Cookie, local storage, and eval commands
remediation.suggestion: Document these commands as sensitive operations and require clear task scope before using them.
Prefer pinned versions and explain that npm, git, and dependency installation execute third-party code.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Workflows with Agent Browser
content.value_statement: AI agents need a reliable way to inspect and operate web pages. Agent Browser provides command-driven navigation, interaction, snapshots, screenshots, and session handling.
actual_capabilities: Opens pages and supports back, forward, reload, and tab navigation.
Clicks, fills, types, selects, uploads files, and sends keyboard events.
Captures page snapshots, screenshots, PDFs, text, HTML, values, and attributes.
Finds elements by role, text, label, placeholder, alt text, title, and test id.
Supports headed mode, named sessions, CDP connections, frames, dialogs, and JSON output.
limitations: Requires installing the agent-browser CLI and browser dependencies before use.
Browser element refs can change after navigation, reloads, or dynamic page updates.
Authenticated profile examples need careful review before use on real accounts.
The skill does not enforce site policies or permission boundaries by itself.

use_cases.title: Smoke Test Web Forms
use_cases.description: Navigate a staging page, fill inputs, submit forms, and report visible validation results.

use_cases.title: Build Agent Browser Loops
use_cases.description: Use snapshots and stable refs to observe a page, choose an action, and verify the result.

use_cases.title: Extract Page State
use_cases.description: Capture page text, titles, URLs, element counts, screenshots, and PDFs for review workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Open and Observe a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Agent Browser to open <url>, capture a snapshot, and summarize the main visible sections. Do not log in or submit forms.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Public Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Agent Browser to inspect the form at <url>, fill safe test values, submit it, and report visible success or validation messages.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Staging Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Agent Browser on my staging URL to complete the specified workflow. Capture snapshots before and after each important action.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Session Run
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan and run an Agent Browser workflow with separate named sessions for two test users. Use only test accounts and report each session state.

output_examples.input: Inspect a dashboard page and report important controls.
output_examples.output: The page opened successfully. Key controls found: navigation menu, search field, status table, filter panel, and export button.

output_examples.input: Run a smoke test on a staging signup form.
output: The form loaded and all required fields were visible.
Safe test values were entered and the submit action completed.
The page displayed a validation message for the test email domain.

output_examples.input: Capture evidence from a product page.
output_examples.output: The workflow captured the page title, current URL, visible price text, main image presence, and a screenshot for review.

best_practices: Use isolated browser sessions and test accounts for automation tasks.
Take a fresh snapshot after each navigation or major page update.
Confirm the target URL and allowed actions before running form submissions.
anti_patterns: Do not attach automation to a real personal browser profile without explicit approval.
Do not use cookie, storage, or eval commands unless the task clearly requires them.
Do not rely on old element refs after navigation or dynamic content changes.

faq.question: What does this skill help an agent do?
faq.answer: It helps an agent operate a browser through structured CLI commands for navigation, interaction, inspection, and screenshots.

faq.question: Does it require a browser installation?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI and its browser dependencies must be installed before the commands can run.

faq.question: Can it work with authenticated sessions?
faq.answer: The documentation describes session support, but real account automation should use isolated test profiles and explicit approval.

faq.question: How should an agent choose elements?
faq.answer: The recommended workflow is to take a snapshot, use the returned refs, act, and then verify with another snapshot.

faq.question: Can it collect screenshots or PDFs?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented commands include screenshots and PDF output for browser pages.

faq.question: Is this only for testing?
faq.answer: No. It can support testing, page inspection, data extraction, and agent workflow development.
